title: Absolute moment of a regular sign sum
statement:
There is a real constant $C\geq0$ such that for every $n\in\mathbb N$, every family of real coefficients $(a_i)_{i\in\mathrm{Fin}\,n}$, and every $\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$, if $\sum_i a_i^2=1$ and $|a_i|\leq\varepsilon$ for every $i$, then
\[\left|\mathbb E\left|\sum_i a_i\sigma(X_i)\right|-\sqrt{2/\pi}\right|\leq C\varepsilon,\]
where $X$ is uniform on the Boolean cube and $\sigma$ is the sign encoding.
hypotheses_covered: The sum of squared coefficients equals $1$
replaced: There exists a universal real constant $C\ge0$ such that for every $n\ge0$, real coefficients $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, and real $\varepsilon$, if $\sum_i a_i^2=1$ and $|a_i|\le\varepsilon$ for all $i$, then $|\mathbb E|\sum_i a_i\xi_i|-\sqrt{2/\pi}|\le C\varepsilon$, where the $\xi_i$ are independent uniform signs.
